title: GPU fabric bisection: tenant-aware lane slicing and progressive eviction for noisy neighbor mitigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: As Dedicated customers run mixed workloads on shared GPU clusters we still observe episodic throughput regressions caused by noisy tenants whose bursty KV-cache usage and oversized batch allocations saturate IO and memory bandwidth. Goal: Implement a tenant bisection and lane-slicing strategy that provides throughput guarantees, enforces per-tenant quotas, and contains noisy neighbors with minimal user-visible degradation. This ticket covers the runtime control-plane changes, autoscaler policy hooks, and quota enforcement surface needed to (1) carve GPU fabric into tenant lanes, (2) apply progressive eviction and soft-quota backpressure, and (3) integrate with predictive autoscale to maintain contract throughput. High-level approach: 1) Tenant-aware lane slicing: introduce logical lane boundaries at the runtime scheduler that partition GPU queues and KV cache segments. Lanes are sized by expected token/sec and can be hard-reserved or soft-shared. 2) Progressive eviction: implement a three-stage eviction policy: (a) adaptive soft-throttle (reduce max batch size, add artificial pacing), (b) KV-cache compaction + prefix eviction, (c) hard eviction of batch requests and queue re-prioritization. Eviction decisions score requests by tenant SLA, queue wait time, and observed bandwidth usage. 3) Quota enforcement: support per-tenant token tokens/sec and burst reservoirs implemented via a hybrid token-bucket + lease mechanism; add observability for current reserves and predicted depletion time. 4) Autoscaling integration: expose lane-level metrics to autoscaler; implement predictive scaling policy that reacts to reservoir exhaustion and sustained demand above lane capacity. 5) Fallbacks and graceful degradation: provide automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants or region-level overflow with rate-limited routing to preserve tail latency. 6) Observability and ops: add per-lane dashboards, alert rules (latency SLO breach, reservoir low, eviction spike), and a playbook for on-call. Considerations and constraints: - Must remain compatible with Dedicated’s isolation SLAs; hard reservations cannot be overcommitted. - Storage and KV-cache compaction should not increase tail latency for good tenants. - Progressive eviction must avoid cascading requeues that amplify tail latency. - Implementation should minimize changes to model execution kernels; most work is in scheduler, cache manager, and autoscaler hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Lane reservation API available via control plane to define hard vs soft lanes for a tenant
Progressive eviction implemented and exercised in unit/integration tests with deterministic scoring
Per-tenant token/sec quota enforcement with burst reservoir and visible metrics
Autoscaler responds to lane exhaustion events in end-to-end e2e test (scale-up within configured SLO)
Performance targets: 95th percentile tail latency degradation < 10% for unaffected tenants during noisy neighbor scenarios
Runbook created and validated by on-call during staged rollout
Conformance test: when a tenant exceeds hard quota, requests are rejected with 429 and documented error codes
